skill.name: write-swift
skill.description: Provides modern Swift 6 guidance for data modeling, concurrency, generics, API design, performance, testing, macros, memory safety, and migrations.
skill.summary: Write, review, and migrate Swift using current language patterns and practical safety guidance.
skill.author: emilkowalski

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-only Swift programming guide with no executable scripts or runtime integrations. All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Swift macros, or ordinary technical prose, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

content.value_statement: Outdated Swift patterns can create concurrency errors, unclear APIs, and avoidable performance costs. This skill provides current Swift 6 guidance for implementation, review, and migration.
actual_capabilities: Recommends value types, ownership models, and error handling patterns for modern Swift.
Explains actor isolation, Sendable, structured concurrency, cancellation, and SwiftUI concurrency.
Guides protocol, generic, opaque type, and existential design decisions.
Reviews performance risks involving allocation, copying, dispatch, ARC, and unsafe memory access.
Creates Swift Testing strategies with expectations, requirements, parameterized tests, traits, and known issues.
Plans incremental Swift 6 migrations with concurrency checking and target-by-target language mode changes.
limitations: The guidance targets Swift 6.3 and marks Swift 6.4 features as unreleased.
It does not run Xcode, compile projects, execute tests, or collect profiling data by itself.
Project deployment targets and framework constraints still require local verification.
Performance recommendations require measurements from representative builds and workloads.

use_cases.title: Build a New Swift Feature
use_cases.description: Choose clear data models, error handling, isolation, and tests before implementing a feature.

use_cases.title: Review a Swift Codebase
use_cases.description: Identify outdated concurrency, abstraction, memory, testing, and performance patterns during code review.

use_cases.title: Migrate to Swift 6
use_cases.description: Sequence compiler upgrades, concurrency checks, warning fixes, and language mode changes across targets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Swift Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Swift model for [domain]. Explain whether each type should be a struct, enum, actor, or class, and state why.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Swift Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Swift function for clarity, error handling, ownership, and modern syntax. Explain each recommended change and respect Swift [version].

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Concurrency Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Swift concurrency error or hang. Trace actor isolation and Sendable boundaries, then propose the smallest data-race-safe correction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Swift 6 Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a target-by-target Swift 6 migration plan for [project]. Prioritize concurrency warnings, preserve behavior, define verification steps, and separate later refactoring.

output_examples.input: Should this shared cache be a class, actor, or value type?
output: Use an actor when multiple tasks must mutate the same cache.
Keep values crossing the actor boundary Sendable.
Recheck cached state after suspension points to handle actor reentrancy.

output_examples.input: Review a function that starts one detached task for every image.
output: Replace detached tasks with a bounded task group.
Preserve cancellation and priority through structured concurrency.
Measure image processing before adding parallel work.

output_examples.input: How should an XCTest suite move to Swift Testing?
output: Keep required UI and performance tests in XCTest.
Write new unit tests with Test, expect, and require.
Migrate existing tests incrementally and preserve independent execution.

best_practices: Provide the Swift version, platform targets, and relevant build settings.
Include compiler diagnostics, surrounding types, and isolation annotations when debugging concurrency.
Profile representative tests before requesting performance-specific changes.
anti_patterns: Do not adopt unreleased Swift features without checking the active toolchain.
Do not silence Sendable errors with unchecked annotations before fixing ownership or isolation.
Do not combine a Swift 6 migration with unrelated architectural refactoring.

faq.question: Which Swift version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Swift 6.3 and clearly identifies Swift 6.4 features that remain unreleased.

faq.question: Can it help fix data-race diagnostics?
faq.answer: Yes. It analyzes sharing, Sendable conformance, actor isolation, task structure, and suspension points.

faq.question: Does it replace compiler and runtime testing?
faq.answer: No. Compile the result and run tests with the project's actual toolchain and deployment targets.

faq.question: Can it review SwiftUI concurrency?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers main actor isolation, Sendable closures, state capture, and task placement in UI workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover performance optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains likely costs and measurement methods, but recommendations require profiling evidence.

faq.question: Can XCTest and Swift Testing coexist?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends incremental migration while retaining XCTest for UI automation, performance metrics, and Objective-C requirements.
